method.name: semantic closure and countermodels
method.description: Trace each proposed property through identity, PlanId, RuleKey, baseline, cancellation, replay, waiver, retention, and threat-model semantics. Distinguish every clean decision's forced property from its preferred mechanism and compare other clean derivations.
method.differentFromAuthor: The author used vocabulary overlap and targeted grep. This review follows semantic responsibility across documents; different words do not prove absence.

summary.headline: The artifact establishes neither eight ONLY-CLEANSHEET gaps nor seven adoptions. Four directions survive only after reclassification and rewrite; four should not enter the architecture.
retainReframed: CS-04 detector-semantic delta in baseline comparison
summary.authority: Nothing is adopted or sealed here. Retained directions are candidate inputs for their owning claims or a coordinator-approved new claim.

perDecision.sourceAssessment: Clean a:D31/D61 force neutralisation of incidental environment and recording of unavoidable semantic differences. Incumbent Snapshot/Plan already record environment inputs and case folding, but equality is promised only under identical environment identities; no ambient-input closure is stated.
perDecision.architectureDirection: Analysis depends only on enumerated semantic inputs. Neutralise or canonicalise locale, collation, timezone, clock, entropy, iteration order, path form, and other incidental ambient state. An environment property that genuinely changes source semantics is explicit in Snapshot/Plan and Coverage; it never changes evidence under one semantic identity.
perDecision.caveat: Do not promise equality across genuinely different target semantics. Case collisions may require an explicit target, typed collision, or indeterminate Coverage.

perDecision.sourceAssessment: Clean a:D13 calls the Datalog-shaped class PREFERRED and its reachability premise unverified. Before clean output, architecture/01 rejected Datalog as a day-one requirement and architecture/09 R-2 deferred the class pending a real schema and representative rules.
perDecision.architectureDirection: Keep declarative rules statically analysable, terminating/budgetable, canonical, and zero-authority. Select recursion, negation, aggregation, and evaluator class only from representative evidence.
perDecision.counterexample: A bounded non-recursive matcher can satisfy every validated day-one rule. Fixpoint recursion would then freeze complexity without a requirement.

perDecision.sourceAssessment: BundleId plus artifact digest identifies exact bytes; artifact digest enters PlanId; delivery requires contribution bundle digest in PlanId; RuleKey hashes rule plus config. A body change is already detected. Clean a:D14 says only one of replay or conformance is forced and the version+digest+corpus triad is PREFERRED.
perDecision.architectureDirection: If baseline evolution needs rule-granular semantic identity, define effective rule semantics over canonical compiled meaning, parameter schema, fact dependencies, and producer semantics, then specify baseline behavior when it changes. Exact bundle bytes remain supply-chain identity.
perDecision.whyDigestAloneFails: A hash over body/schema/dependencies detects content change but cannot prove behavior changed or stayed equivalent. Renaming it a behavior digest does not close upgrade trust.

perDecision.sourceAssessment: Clean a:D38/D39 explicitly mark pending-adoption and replay PREFERRED. Clean b:D19 independently forces detection-delta versus code-delta. Incumbent handles fingerprint-recipe incompatibility but not effective rule-set or rule-semantics change with unchanged source.
perDecision.architectureDirection: Baseline comparison distinguishes code delta from detector/rule semantic delta. Findings caused solely by a changed or newly activated semantic input cannot be silently called code-net-new. A mismatch yields a typed no-comparison, pending-adoption, or explicit-adoption state under declared policy.
openChoices: whether new-rule findings gate immediately, remain loud/non-gating, or make comparison indeterminate
whether replay, conformance, dual evaluation, or explicit adoption proves compatibility
behavior when historical inputs or producer closure are unavailable offline
perDecision.confidence: high on the distinction; medium on final policy

perDecision.sourceAssessment: Incumbent already has per-ExecutionId cancellation. Clean a:D23 says cancellation is forced but coalescing PREFERRED; b:D10 also marks superseding PREFERRED; c:D19 permits sharing only identical immutable task keys with reference-counted cancellation.
perDecision.counterexample: A CI run, human audit, and agent query overlap on different snapshots/scopes. Workspace latest-wins cancels required work merely because a later request arrived, so one client's completion depends on another's timing.
perDecision.architectureDirection: Bound admission and isolate cancellation per ExecutionId. Deduplicate only identical immutable semantic task keys, and never let one caller cancel another caller's required work. Measure queue policy.

perDecision.sourceAssessment: Incumbent already separates verification, replay, and attestation; requires full offline derivation closure for replay; and requires EvidenceDigest equality under identical deterministic inputs and exact Coverage. A command and exact enum are detailed surface choices.
perDecision.counterexample: Same findings but different proof edges under identical pinned semantics is a determinism defect or bad digest scope. Calling it equivalent conceals the failure.
perDecision.architectureDirection: Pinned-semantics replay is identical or divergent, with typed unavailable/unsupported reasons. Cross-version compatibility may use an explicit versioned equivalence relation but is not deterministic reproduction.

perDecision.sourceAssessment: Incumbent makes waivers tracked project intent applied by host policy after findings. It omits target precision, applied-waiver evidence, silent widening, and stale/unused handling. Clean a:D18 marks existence/syntax PREFERRED but recorded-not-hidden forced once suppression exists.
perDecision.architectureDirection: A waiver never deletes a finding or evidence. It is a versioned policy input with an explicit target; application is verdict evidence. It cannot silently widen to future rules/subjects; stale, unmatched, ambiguous, and scope-drift states are reportable and cannot silently suppress.

perDecision.sourceAssessment: Incumbent separates rebuildable cache from evidence, evicts cache first, defines reachability collection, protects pinned evidence from cache GC, and exposes purge. It lacks a finite cache capacity and deliberate user reclamation policy. Threat-model R5 requires inventory and real deletion.
perDecision.architectureDirection: Rebuildable cache has an enforced finite resource policy and is safe to evict without changing evidence or verdict semantics. Evidence pins are separate. Users can inventory and reclaim cache; deletion reports removals and retained pins.
perDecision.defer: Exact command, size/age defaults, eviction algorithm, and capacity numbers.

findings.title: Vocabulary grep creates false ONLY-CLEANSHEET classifications
findings.detail: CS-02 was addressed and deferred; CS-03 is partly discharged by artifact digest/PlanId/RuleKey; CS-07 already has host-owned waivers; CS-08 already has cache/evidence separation and safe eviction. Different vocabulary is not absence.
findings.requiredChange: Classify semantic proposition and responsibility closure; record incumbent partials and divergences.

findings.title: Seven adopted and zero unresolved are unauthorized metrics
findings.detail: Six rows say ADOPT-CANDIDATE, the artifact is unreviewed, and ratification remains required. CS-04 has product policy choices, CS-05 is measurement-gated, and CS-07 has product/UX choices. Candidates are not adopted or resolved.
findings.requiredChange: Report proposed, retained, rejected, product-owned, measurement-gated, and unresolved separately.

findings.title: Justification Test fields are circular, not requirements
findings.detail: CS-03 through CS-08 say independent derivation plus incumbent absence is the requirement. That is provenance evidence, not a user/system requirement and does not establish merit.
findings.requiredChange: State the product/system requirement and a countermodel or rejected alternative for each proposal.

findings.title: Content drift detection is conflated with baseline semantic evolution
findings.detail: Exact artifact identity already detects bytes changing. A body/schema/dependency digest cannot establish behavioral equivalence. The real gap is how baseline comparison treats changed detector semantics and distinguishes detector delta from code delta.
findings.requiredChange: Rehome to VERSIONING/baseline policy before choosing replay, conformance, or pending-adoption.

findings.title: Workspace latest-wins violates first-class client and attempt isolation
findings.detail: Different snapshots/scopes/clients overlap. Cancelling earlier work solely because a later request exists lets timing alter another client's completion; the clean source calls coalescing PREFERRED.
findings.requiredChange: Permit sharing only for identical immutable task keys with reference-counted cancellation; measure scheduling.

findings.title: Equivalent reproduction weakens determinism
findings.detail: Under identical pinned semantics, changed evidence with equal findings is divergence. Compatibility across versions is a distinct operation with a versioned relation.
findings.requiredChange: Keep pinned replay binary and place cross-version equivalence in VERSIONING.

findings.title: Proposed gaps mix architecture with command/syntax design
findings.detail: A reproduce command, inline syntax, GC command, scheduler, and exact evaluator are mechanisms below the guarantee. Adopting them would reverse the altitude correction without a named consumer choice.
findings.requiredChange: Retain only environment closure, semantic-delta honesty, waiver non-hiding/non-widening, and finite safe cache at architecture altitude.

resolves.CS-03: REJECT AS STATED — drift already detected; merge semantic mismatch into CS-04.
resolves.CS-04: ACCEPT REFRAMED AS OPEN POLICY — detector delta cannot silently become code-net-new.
resolves.CS-05: REJECT LATEST-WINS — cancellation yes; scheduler preferred and measured.
resolves.CS-06: REJECT AS ARCHITECTURE GAP — exact replay binary; compatibility elsewhere.
resolves.CS-07: PARTIAL ACCEPT — waiver auditability/non-widening; UX deferred.
resolves.CS-08: PARTIAL ACCEPT — finite safe reclaim strengthens existing cache design.

knownLimitations: Not the complete clean-sheet inventory/crosswalk required by B-ADJ-01.
No representative workload establishes coalescing policy, cache capacity, or new-rule adoption default.
No coordinator/product choice is made for waiver UX, new-rule gate policy, or retention defaults.
Wire schemas and commands are deliberately not designed.
confidence: high on CS-02/03/05/06 and CS-01/04/08 cores; medium-high on minimum waiver obligations
